title: Was early New York jazz less "black"?
summary: Carter agrees early New York music was less black but says musicians then did not think about racial roots.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, there's another point, that a lot of -- I'll put this in a very general way -- a lot of the music that was recorded early in New York; some of the early Fletcher Henderson for example; the orchestra and not so much the accompanying groups that were accompanying the vocalists and the blues singers and so forth -- seems, some people would claim, much less 'black' whatever that might mean than, say, the music that was coming out of Chicago from people recently from New Orleans, and indeed, seems a lot less black than a lot of the jazz music of today.
Would you care to respond to that?
I guess I would agree with that. Yes, I guess I would agree with that, Jim. What else can I say in response to that?
Well, I don't know -- maybe we could pursue that a little.
I don't know -- how did musicians

regard themselves in terms of racial orientation or their music in relation to racial consciousness or racial background? Was there much thought paid to this? I mean was there much talk or much emphasis on one kind of music being black music as opposed to some other kind of music which wasn't black music, or is that a much more recent attitude?

Well, there wasn't as much talk about it at that time, and probably not as much thought about it as there is now. You know? I think everybody was just trying to do their thing without a great deal of thought about what was black or Afro American or jazz, you know, quote, unquote. I think everybody was just trying to play what they heard, what they felt, without even thinking in terms of roots, as we talk about now, you know.
Yes, blues roots, church roots ... 's to what exactly. That is which I allude, when I say that. Yes. And I think that's about the way it was, and I have nothing against this.
Can you finish your sentence? I think we're gonna have to make a modulation here on the tape.
I'll resume on the other side.
